passages.text: I speak the truth in Christ; I am not lying, as confirmed by my conscience in the Holy Spirit.
passages.sermon:
Paul is the speaker.
\r\nPaul speaks as a Christian apostle.
\r\nPaul says, “I speak the truth in Christ.”
\r\nPaul does not lie.
\r\nPaul’s conscience confirms this.
\r\nThe Holy Spirit works in Paul’s conscience.
passages.original: Ἀλήθειαν λέγω ἐν Χριστῷ οὐ ψεύδομαι συμμαρτυρούσης μοι τῆς συνειδήσεώς μου ἐν Πνεύματι Ἁγίῳ

passages.text: I have deep sorrow and unceasing anguish in my heart.
passages.sermon:
Paul is the speaker.
Paul is a Christian apostle.
Paul feels deep sorrow.
Paul has unceasing anguish in his heart.
passages.original: ὅτι λύπη μοί ἐστιν μεγάλη καὶ ἀδιάλειπτος ὀδύνη τῇ καρδίᾳ μου

passages.text: For I could wish that I myself were cursed and cut off from Christ for the sake of my brothers, my own flesh and blood, the people of Israel. Theirs is the adoption as sons; theirs the divine glory and the covenants; theirs the giving of the law, the temple worship, and the promises.
passages.sermon:
Paul is the speaker.
Paul is a Jew.
Paul loves his fellow Israelites.
Paul wishes he could be cursed and cut off from Christ.
Paul would do this for the sake of his brothers.
His brothers are his own people by birth.
His brothers are the people of Israel.
The people of Israel have received adoption as sons.
The people of Israel have received the divine glory.
The people of Israel have received the covenants.
The people of Israel have received the giving of the law.
The people of Israel have received temple worship.
The people of Israel have received the promises.
passages.original: ηὐχόμην γὰρ ἀνάθεμα εἶναι αὐτὸς ἐγὼ ἀπὸ τοῦ Χριστοῦ ὑπὲρ τῶν ἀδελφῶν μου τῶν συγγενῶν μου κατὰ σάρκα οἵτινές εἰσιν Ἰσραηλῖται ὧν ἡ υἱοθεσία καὶ ἡ δόξα καὶ αἱ διαθῆκαι καὶ ἡ νομοθεσία καὶ ἡ λατρεία καὶ αἱ ἐπαγγελίαι

passages.text: Theirs are the patriarchs, and from them proceeds the human descent of Christ, who is God over all, forever worthy of praise! Amen.
passages.sermon:
The people of Israel have the patriarchs.
The patriarchs are their ancestors.
Christ came from the people of Israel in his human nature.
Christ is God over all.
Christ is forever worthy of praise.
Amen.
passages.original: ὧν οἱ πατέρες καὶ ἐξ ὧν ὁ Χριστὸς τὸ κατὰ σάρκα ὁ ὢν ἐπὶ πάντων Θεὸς εὐλογητὸς εἰς τοὺς αἰῶνας ἀμήν

passages.text: It is not as though God’s word has failed. For not all who are descended from Israel are Israel.
passages.sermon: God’s word has not failed.\r\nNot everyone descended from Israel truly belongs to Israel.
passages.original: Οὐχ οἷον δὲ ὅτι ἐκπέπτωκεν ὁ λόγος τοῦ Θεοῦ οὐ γὰρ πάντες οἱ ἐξ Ἰσραήλ οὗτοι Ἰσραήλ

passages.text: Nor because they are Abraham’s descendants are they all his children. On the contrary, “Through Isaac your offspring will be reckoned.”
passages.sermon:
Not all people who descend from Abraham are his true children.
God does not count every physical descendant as a child.
God said, “Through Isaac your offspring will be counted.”
God chose Isaac, not every descendant, to carry the promise.
passages.original: οὐδ’ ὅτι εἰσὶν σπέρμα Ἀβραάμ πάντες τέκνα ἀλλ’ Ἐν Ἰσαὰκ κληθήσεταί σοι σπέρμα

passages.text: So it is not the children of the flesh who are God’s children, but it is the children of the promise who are regarded as offspring.
passages.sermon:
God chooses His children.
God does not choose by physical descent.
Children born by natural means are not automatically God’s children.
God calls the children of the promise His true children.
God regards the children of the promise as His offspring.
passages.original: τοῦτ’ ἔστιν οὐ τὰ τέκνα τῆς σαρκὸς ταῦτα τέκνα τοῦ Θεοῦ ἀλλὰ τὰ τέκνα τῆς ἐπαγγελίας λογίζεται εἰς σπέρμα

passages.text: For this is what the promise stated: “At the appointed time I will return, and Sarah will have a son.”
passages.sermon:
God made a promise.
God spoke this promise clearly.
God said, “At the appointed time, I will return.”
God said, “Sarah will have a son.”
passages.original: ἐπαγγελίας γὰρ ὁ λόγος οὗτος Κατὰ τὸν καιρὸν τοῦτον ἐλεύσομαι καὶ ἔσται τῇ Σάρρᾳ υἱός

passages.text: Not only that, but Rebecca’s children were conceived by one man, our father Isaac.
passages.sermon:
Rebecca was the wife of Isaac.
Isaac is our father.
Rebecca had children by Isaac alone.
Rebecca’s children came from one man.
passages.original: Οὐ μόνον δέ ἀλλὰ καὶ Ῥεβέκκα ἐξ ἑνὸς κοίτην ἔχουσα Ἰσαὰκ τοῦ πατρὸς ἡμῶν

passages.text: Yet before the twins were born or had done anything good or bad, in order that God’s plan of election might stand, not by works but by Him who calls, she was told, “The older will serve the younger.”
passages.sermon:
God chose Isaac and Rebecca to be the parents of twins.
The twins were not yet born.
The twins had not done anything good or bad.
God wanted His plan of choosing people to remain.
God’s plan does not depend on human works.
God’s plan depends on God, who calls people.
God told Rebecca a message.
God said, “The older will serve the younger.”
passages.original: μήπω γὰρ γεννηθέντων μηδὲ πραξάντων τι ἀγαθὸν ἢ φαῦλον ἵνα ἡ κατ’ ἐκλογὴν πρόθεσις τοῦ Θεοῦ μένῃ οὐκ ἐξ ἔργων ἀλλ’ ἐκ τοῦ καλοῦντος ἐρρέθη αὐτῇ ὅτι Ὁ μείζων δουλεύσει τῷ ἐλάσσονι

passages.text: So it is written: “Jacob I loved, but Esau I hated.”
passages.sermon: God spoke these words in Scripture.\r\nGod said, “I loved Jacob.”\r\nGod also said, “I hated Esau.”
passages.original: καθὼς γέγραπται Τὸν Ἰακὼβ ἠγάπησα τὸν δὲ Ἠσαῦ ἐμίσησα

passages.text: What then shall we say? Is God unjust? Certainly not!
passages.sermon:
God is always just.
God never acts with injustice.
We must not say that God is unjust.
God’s actions are always right.
God never does wrong.
We should never accuse God of injustice.
passages.original: Τί οὖν ἐροῦμεν μὴ ἀδικία παρὰ τῷ θεῷ μὴ γένοιτο

passages.text: For He says to Moses: “I will have mercy on whom I have mercy, and I will have compassion on whom I have compassion.”
passages.sermon: God spoke to Moses.\r\nGod said, “I will show mercy to anyone I choose.”\r\nGod also said, “I will show compassion to anyone I choose.”
passages.original: τῷ Μωϋσεῖ γὰρ λέγει Ἐλεήσω ὃν ἂν ἐλεῶ καὶ οἰκτιρήσω ὃν ἂν οἰκτίρω

passages.text: So then, it does not depend on man’s desire or effort, but on God’s mercy.
passages.sermon:
God decides to show mercy.
God’s mercy does not depend on what a person wants.
God’s mercy does not depend on what a person does.
God alone gives mercy.
passages.original: Ἄρα οὖν οὐ τοῦ θέλοντος οὐδὲ τοῦ τρέχοντος ἀλλὰ τοῦ ἐλεῶντος Θεοῦ

passages.text: For the Scripture says to Pharaoh: “I raised you up for this very purpose, that I might display My power in you, and that My name might be proclaimed in all the earth.”
passages.sermon:
The Scripture speaks to Pharaoh.
God addresses Pharaoh directly.
God says, “I raised you up for this reason.”
God chose Pharaoh for a specific purpose.
God says, “I want to show My power in you.”
God intends to display His power through Pharaoh.
God says, “I want My name to be proclaimed in all the earth.”
God’s purpose is to make His name known everywhere.
God uses Pharaoh to reveal His power and spread His name throughout the world.
passages.original: λέγει γὰρ ἡ γραφὴ τῷ Φαραὼ ὅτι Εἰς αὐτὸ τοῦτο ἐξήγειρά σε ὅπως ἐνδείξωμαι ἐν σοὶ τὴν δύναμίν μου καὶ ὅπως διαγγελῇ τὸ ὄνομά μου ἐν πάσῃ τῇ γῇ

passages.text: Therefore God has mercy on whom He wants to have mercy, and He hardens whom He wants to harden.
passages.sermon:
God acts according to His own will.
God chooses to show mercy to some people.
God chooses to harden the hearts of other people.
God decides whom to show mercy.
God decides whom to harden.
No one else controls God's choices.
passages.original: ἄρα οὖν ὃν θέλει ἐλεεῖ ὃν δὲ θέλει σκληρύνει

passages.text: One of you will say to me, “Then why does God still find fault? For who can resist His will?”
passages.sermon:
Paul writes to the Christians in Rome.
Paul teaches about God's authority and choices.
Someone may ask Paul a question.
The person says, “Why does God still find fault?”
The person also says, “Who can resist God’s will?”
passages.original: Ἐρεῖς μοι οὖν Τί οὖν ἔτι μέμφεται τῷ γὰρ βουλήματι αὐτοῦ τίς ἀνθέστηκεν

passages.text: But who are you, O man, to talk back to God? Shall what is formed say to Him who formed it, “Why did You make me like this?”
passages.sermon:
God is the Creator.
God forms every person.
You are a human being.
You are not the Creator.
You cannot answer back to God.
A created thing cannot question its Maker.
A formed thing cannot say to the one who formed it, "Why did you make me this way?"
passages.original: ὦ ἄνθρωπε μενοῦνγε σὺ τίς εἶ ὁ ἀνταποκρινόμενος τῷ Θεῷ μὴ ἐρεῖ τὸ πλάσμα τῷ πλάσαντι Τί με ἐποίησας οὕτως

passages.text: Does not the potter have the right to make from the same lump of clay one vessel for special occasions and another for common use?
passages.sermon:
God is like a potter.
God shapes people as a potter shapes clay.
The potter uses one lump of clay.
The potter makes one vessel for special honor.
The potter makes another vessel for common use.
The potter has the right to do this.
God has the right to do this with people.
passages.original: ἢ οὐκ ἔχει ἐξουσίαν ὁ κεραμεὺς τοῦ πηλοῦ ἐκ τοῦ αὐτοῦ φυράματος ποιῆσαι ὃ μὲν εἰς τιμὴν σκεῦος ὃ δὲ εἰς ἀτιμίαν

passages.text: What if God, intending to show His wrath and make His power known, bore with great patience the vessels of His wrath, prepared for destruction?
passages.sermon:
God is all-powerful.
God sometimes wants to show His anger.
God sometimes wants to make His power known.
God endures some people with great patience.
These people are like vessels of His wrath.
God has prepared these people for destruction.
God patiently bears with them.
passages.original: Εἰ δὲ θέλων ὁ Θεὸς ἐνδείξασθαι τὴν ὀργὴν καὶ γνωρίσαι τὸ δυνατὸν αὐτοῦ ἤνεγκεν ἐν πολλῇ μακροθυμίᾳ σκεύη ὀργῆς κατηρτισμένα εἰς ἀπώλειαν

passages.text: What if He did this to make the riches of His glory known to the vessels of His mercy, whom He prepared in advance for glory— including us, whom He has called not only from the Jews, but also from the Gentiles?
passages.sermon:
God wants to show the riches of His glory.
God shows this glory to the vessels of His mercy.
God prepared these vessels of mercy in advance for glory.
We are these vessels of mercy.
God called us.
God did not call only people from the Jews.
God also called people from the Gentiles.
passages.original: καὶ ἵνα γνωρίσῃ τὸν πλοῦτον τῆς δόξης αὐτοῦ ἐπὶ σκεύη ἐλέους ἃ προητοίμασεν εἰς δόξαν οὓς καὶ ἐκάλεσεν ἡμᾶς οὐ μόνον ἐξ Ἰουδαίων ἀλλὰ καὶ ἐξ ἐθνῶν

passages.text: As He says in Hosea: “I will call them ‘My People’ who are not My people, and I will call her ‘My Beloved’ who is not My beloved,” and, “It will happen that in the very place where it was said to them, ‘You are not My people,’ they will be called ‘sons of the living God.’ ”
passages.sermon:
God spoke through the prophet Hosea.
God said, “I will call people ‘My People’ who were not My people.”
God said, “I will call a woman ‘My Beloved’ who was not My beloved.”
God said, “In the place where I said, ‘You are not My people,’ they will be called ‘sons of the living God.’”
passages.original: ὡς καὶ ἐν τῷ Ὡσηὲ λέγει Καλέσω τὸν οὐ λαόν μου λαόν μου καὶ τὴν οὐκ ἠγαπημένην ἠγαπημένην Καὶ Ἔσται ἐν τῷ τόπῳ οὗ ἐρρέθη αὐτοῖς Οὐ λαός μου ὑμεῖς ἐκεῖ κληθήσονται Υἱοὶ Θεοῦ ζῶντος

passages.text: Isaiah cries out concerning Israel: “Though the number of the Israelites is like the sand of the sea, only the remnant will be saved.
passages.sermon:
Isaiah speaks about Israel.
He says, “The people of Israel are very many.
They are as many as the sand by the sea.
But only a small group will be saved.”
passages.original: Ἠσαΐας δὲ κράζει ὑπὲρ τοῦ Ἰσραήλ Ἐὰν ᾖ ὁ ἀριθμὸς τῶν υἱῶν Ἰσραὴλ ὡς ἡ ἄμμος τῆς θαλάσσης τὸ ὑπόλειμμα σωθήσεται

passages.text: For the Lord will carry out His sentence on the earth thoroughly and decisively.”
passages.sermon:
The Lord will act on the earth.
He will finish His work completely.
He will do it quickly and decisively.
He will carry out His sentence with finality.
passages.original: λόγον γὰρ συντελῶν καὶ συντέμνων ποιήσει Κύριος ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς

passages.text: It is just as Isaiah foretold: “Unless the Lord of Hosts had left us descendants, we would have become like Sodom, we would have resembled Gomorrah.”
passages.sermon:
Isaiah was a prophet of God.
Isaiah spoke about Israel.
Isaiah said something important about the people of Israel.
He said, “Unless the Lord of Hosts had left us descendants, we would have become like Sodom.
We would have resembled Gomorrah.”
Sodom and Gomorrah were cities destroyed for their sin.
Isaiah meant that God saved a remnant of Israel.
God did not let all of Israel be destroyed.
God showed mercy by leaving descendants.
passages.original: Καὶ καθὼς προείρηκεν Ἠσαΐας Εἰ μὴ Κύριος Σαβαὼθ ἐγκατέλιπεν ἡμῖν σπέρμα ὡς Σόδομα ἂν ἐγενήθημεν καὶ ὡς Γόμορρα ἂν ὡμοιώθημεν

passages.text: What then will we say? That the Gentiles, who did not pursue righteousness, have obtained it, a righteousness that is by faith; but Israel, who pursued a law of righteousness, has not attained it.
passages.sermon:
Paul speaks to the church in Rome.
Paul asks a question.
He says, “What then will we say?”
The Gentiles did not pursue righteousness.
The Gentiles have obtained righteousness.
This righteousness comes by faith.
Israel pursued a law of righteousness.
Israel did not attain the law.
Israel did not reach righteousness through the law.
passages.original: Τί οὖν ἐροῦμεν ὅτι ἔθνη τὰ μὴ διώκοντα δικαιοσύνην κατέλαβεν δικαιοσύνην δικαιοσύνην δὲ τὴν ἐκ πίστεως Ἰσραὴλ δὲ διώκων νόμον δικαιοσύνης εἰς νόμον οὐκ ἔφθασεν

passages.text: Why not? Because their pursuit was not by faith, but as if it were by works. They stumbled over the stumbling stone, as it is written: “See, I lay in Zion a stone of stumbling and a rock of offense; and the one who believes in Him will never be put to shame.”
passages.sermon:
Israel pursued righteousness by works, not by faith.
They did not seek righteousness through trust in God.
They tried to earn righteousness by their own efforts.
Because of this, they stumbled.
They stumbled over the stone God placed in Zion.
God said, “I lay in Zion a stone that causes people to stumble.
I place a rock that makes people fall.”
Anyone who believes in this stone will not be put to shame.
This stone refers to Jesus Christ.
Those who trust in Jesus will never be disappointed.
passages.original: διὰ τί ὅτι οὐκ ἐκ πίστεως ἀλλ’ ὡς ἐξ ἔργων προσέκοψαν τῷ λίθῳ τοῦ προσκόμματος καθὼς γέγραπται Ἰδοὺ τίθημι ἐν Σιὼν λίθον προσκόμματος καὶ πέτραν σκανδάλου καὶ ὁ πιστεύων ἐπ’ αὐτῷ οὐ καταισχυνθήσεται
